narrative.overview: The interface is a drafting table, not a marketing page. Every screen is built from cool drafting paper, near-black drafting ink, hairline rules, and line-weight depth; soft shadows are absent. Two accents carry all meaning: signal red (#b02a1e) for load and tension, structural steel blue (#1f5c8a) for members, fit, and balance. Labels and data are set in a true monospace (JetBrains Mono) so they read as engineering callouts; headings are set in a serif display (Archivo) so they read as load-bearing frames. Corners are near-square, with a 4px radius as the nominal corner and 8px as the ceiling. The system's density is high but legible: one page holds ten views and two interactive instruments, so hierarchy is carried by line weight, rule placement, and the mono/serif split rather than by color or size alone. Motion is short (160–220ms) and functional; prefers-reduced-motion collapses all of it.
keyCharacteristics: Drafting paper + hairline rules + line-weight depth, no soft shadows.
Dual accents only: signal red (load/tension) and steel blue (member/fit).
True monospace for labels and data; serif display for headings; Inter for body.
Near-square corners; a 4px radius is the nominal corner.
Tabular numerals throughout; CJK fallbacks behind every Latin face.
Content density with engineering annotation instead of decoration.

rules.name: The Two-Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal red and steel blue are the only hues with semantic weight. Any new color must carry meaning; decoration never gets a new hue.

rules.name: The Rarity Rule
rules.body: Signal red is used on ≤10% of any screen; its scarcity is what makes equilibrium land.

rules.name: The 11px Floor Rule
rules.body: No text drops below 11px; micro-labels floor at 12px (--type-micro) and body copy at 16px (--type-body). The 11px value exists only for in-SVG diagram captions and ranks.

rules.name: The Mono-Annotation Rule
rules.body: Labels, data, ranks, and values are JetBrains Mono uppercase with 0.08em tracking; prose headings and summaries are Archivo serif. The two voices never merge: a heading is never a mono tag, a data value is never a serif.

rules.name: The No-Soft-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No blurred shadows. Every elevation state is a hard 1–2px offset or a solid ring; blur radius is always 0.

dos: Do use the 6-hex drafting palette only: #e7eaee, #dbe0e6, #f5f6f8, #16181d, #3c434c, #535b65, plus #c3cad3/#8d98a6 hairlines and the three semantic accents #b02a1e/#8c2016/#1f5c8a/#8a5a00.
Do convey depth with hairlines and 1–2px hard line-weight offsets, never a blurred shadow.
Do keep corners at 4px nominal (2px small, 8px maximum).
Do set labels, data, ranks, and values in JetBrains Mono uppercase with 0.08em tracking.
Do put accent emphasis on a 3px top rule or a 1px full ring.
Do keep tabular numerals on all data.
Do respect the 11px floor and the 12px micro / 16px body defaults.
donts: Don't use soft or blurred shadows; blur radius is always 0.
Don't round past 8px or use pill shapes.
Don't add a colored left/right border thicker than 1px; accent weight lives on top edges and full rings.
Don't hardcode secrets, inline styles, or inline scripts; the CSP is default-deny and the site makes no network calls.
Don't introduce a new hue without a semantic meaning.
Don't set a data value in serif or a prose heading in mono.
